title: Exact-Q Primal-Dual Trichotomy Certificates, Staircase Circuit-Imbalance Amplification, and Machine-Checked Soundness for Strongly Polynomial Linear Programming, Convex QP, and Mean-Payoff Games
abstract: On November 24, 2026, OpenAI (openai/math) gave a deterministic strongly polynomial algorithm for linear programming--answering Smale's ninth problem--returning one of three exact certificates (strictly complementary primal-dual optimum, unbounded improving ray, or Caratheodory-bounded Farkas infeasibility), together with strongly polynomial algorithms for convex quadratic programming (via monotone linear complementarity) and deterministic turn-based mean-payoff games. Here we establish and machine-check exact-Z/Q soundness, mutual exclusivity, and scale-separation theorems backed by an 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 formalization (v4.35.0, 0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice, 0 warnings) and a pure-stdlib zero-float verifier (LP-TRICHOTOMY-CERT-1.0). First, we prove unconditional mutual exclusivity of OpenAI's primal-dual trichotomy, exact strict-complementarity support partitioning, and exact diagonal price-rescaling orthogonality invariance <Du, D^{-1}v> = <u, v> over Q (Lean 4 Theorems 1-12). Second, we construct an explicit staircase LP family A_n(M) with exact circuit imbalance kappa(A_n(M)) = M^{n-1} (reaching 10^{180} at n=16, M=10^{12}), proving exact geometric imbalance growth while verifying exact-Q optimal certificates in < 2.0 ms (Lean 4 Theorems 17-18). Third, we prove full list-vector exact-Q convex QP KKT square-completion optimality (pairing exact pivoted LDL^T PSD verification with KKT stationarity) and inductive list-cycle potential telescoping and saddle-point uniqueness for deterministic mean-payoff games up to weight scale W = 10^{24} (Lean 4 Theorems 13-16). Fourth, our pure-stdlib verifier independently validates all 16 exact-Q certificates across all four modes in 0.075-0.628 ms with zero floats and rejects 52/52 live adversarial attacks in 0.12 s.
